0.content:
In the Archon War, Morax defeated the god who had enslaved Xiao, freed him and named him: "Xiao" is the name of a spirit from another land's fables who endured great suffering, as he had. Xiao has served Liyue ever since to repay that debt and will not forgive anyone who speaks against Rex Lapis. When the Traveler told him of Rex Lapis's "death" in 1.0, he said he could not imagine a Liyue without him, but went to rally the other adepti anyway: "Our god is the God of Contracts after all."

After learning that Zhongli is Rex Lapis, he asked the Traveler what Zhongli does all day and tried to find meaning in birds, antiques and flowers. Zhongli, in turn, still worries about him: he asked the Traveler to deliver a powerful remedy to "the young adeptus of Guili Plains". Before going into the Chasm in 2.7, Xiao told Zhongli of his plan, and a swirl of Geo energy caught him when he fell. In 4.4 (limited event) he helped Zhongli test kites for Hu Tao.

1.comment: Xiao: The flute on the wind
1.content: Once, after fighting from dusk until dawn, Xiao collapsed as the gods' hatred overwhelmed him. Then the pain vanished: a clear flute melody, carried over mountains and rivers on the wind, played until first light and gave him a moment's peace. He did not seek the player, already half-sure who it must be, since only one of The Seven could help him. The official Yakshas teaser shows Venti playing. Xiao's own line about Venti ("So that's the name he goes by. His tunes are... forget it.") shows he knows who Venti really is.

2.content:
The yakshas were fierce illuminated beasts whom Morax called on to purge plagues, curses and miasmas spawned by the defeated gods. Five were foremost: Bosacius (the eldest and their leader), Indarias, Bonanus, Menogias and Alatus. Their work fed karmic debt into their souls; some succumbed to rage or madness, some turned on each other, some vanished. Bonanus, Indarias and Menogias died, and Bosacius grew weary, left his treasures in Minlin and disappeared. Only Xiao remains.

When Paimon cried over the book about them, Xiao told her the Yakshas need no sympathy, that his fallen comrades would see her tears as a stain on their legacy, and called the book "fan fiction". Statues of yakshas subduing demons still stand in Liyue, their faces destroyed; a Sumeru folklore text lists offerings and chants once used to appease suffering yakshas.

3.comment: Xiao: Bosacius and the Chasm (Perilous Trail)
3.content: In 2.7 Xiao went into the Chasm's depths seeking his missing brother-in-arms Bosacius, having told only Zhongli. There he crossed paths with the Traveler, Yanfei, Yelan, Itto and Shinobu, all trapped in an illusory domain that fed on their fears. When the Traveler called his name he did not come, because the domain had snared him too; they dragged him out just in time. He confirmed that Bosacius was the Nameless Yaksha who fought with the Millelith during the cataclysm, and purged a remnant of his memory. He offered to spend all his power lifting the others out while staying behind himself; they refused. In the end he powered an illusory Fantastic Compass's platform and, with his last strength, hurled them to the surface. Zhongli's Geo energy caught him as he fell.

4.content:
In his Story Quest (1.3), monsters near Wangshu Inn mutated because of Xiao's accumulated karma. He admitted his karma had caused the trouble, then cleansed the Karma-Heavy Cavern with the Bane of All Evil. A fake adeptus, "Starsnatcher", was drawing more demons with a Sigil of Permission, so Xiao used the Dream Trawler art to summon his soul into a dream. The Traveler collected a censer and lamps from a shrine guarded by the spirit of Pervases, a junior yaksha who sent Xiao his regards and missed Grilled Tiger Fish. Starsnatcher turned out to be Wang Ping'an, a folklorist's grandson and a fan of the Vigilant Yaksha, and he swore to reform. Xiao then ordered Grilled Tiger Fish instead of Almond Tofu, in honour of his old friend.

In the Hereafter World Quest (2.4), Xiao was at Pervases's run-down temple when Paimon asked why no one tended it; he said the Yakshas did not do their duty for recognition. Wang Ping'an later restored the temple and stayed to write a book about the Vigilant Yaksha.

5.content:
The Qixing built Wangshu Inn at Dihua Marsh as a base for Xiao; Verr Goldet and Huai'an, who run it, are Qixing agents who support him. He stops by for Almond Tofu, the one human food he can stomach, whose texture recalls the dreams he once ate. Verr Goldet says he is seldom in a good enough mood to see anyone, and she has never seen him smile. He left a harmless ghost, Dusky Ming, in their care until she can move on. The staff quietly cover for damage when his night-time battles shake the inn.

At Lantern Rite (1.3, limited event) the Traveler and Huai'an set up a festival stall below the inn to bring the festival to him. Yelan's clan says their ancestor's madness eased only near Wangshu Inn. When Zibai began explaining the original meaning of "Wangshu", Xiao finished it for her: the goddess who rides the bright moon's chariot.

6.content:
By slaughtering the endless manifestations of the vengeful gods, Xiao shattered their hatred into fragments that tainted his own soul. The resulting karmic debt can consume flesh, bone and soul. He hears the voices of the dead constantly, demanding more death. It also spreads: it mutates nearby monsters and is dangerous to mortals, whose souls are weaker than adepti's. That is why he avoids people. Mortal medicine has no effect on it.

Relief has come from outside: the flute on the wind, Almond Tofu, and the Traveler's company (by his own admission the pain has eased since he met them). He still insists it is his own doing and his alone to bear.

7.comment: Xiao: The Traveler and "speak my name"
7.content:
Xiao first told the Traveler to leave: mortal blood cannot bear so much adeptal energy. He softened after they helped him again and again. His standing promise is that if they are in danger they should speak his name and he will come. He says the bond between them is now too strong to sever, that he would like to know more about them, and that if the darkness ever took them, ending it would fall to him.

In the Serenitea Pot he admits the comfort is unfamiliar, that he can never have a carefree life, yet accepts their kindness and offers to visit Liyue Harbor with them to understand their world, promising to "speak as little as possible". His yearly letters (2021-2026) bring crystalflies for their hair, an adeptal turquoise for protection, a confession that he dreams of ordinary outings with them, and a bird for them to name.

8.content: Ganyu, half-qilin and half-human, trained under Xiao, who is said to be strict but effective. He sees her as neither mortal nor illuminated beast, wandering both realms with duty as her only guide, and doubts that a Yaksha who knows only slaughter could be a fit mentor for her. She finds him socially distant and stays wary of him, because everyone he ever agreed to team up with is gone.

9.comment: Xiao: Lantern Rite and the Nuo Dance
9.content:
Many Liyue festivals began as imitations of the adepti's victories over man-eating monsters. The buried gods' hatred erupts hardest during the Lantern Rite, so Xiao fights day and night throughout it with the "Nuo Dance of Evil Conquering". That is why he hates the festival, even as the lanterns rising over the safe harbor stir something in him he cannot name.

During the 1.3 Lantern Rite event, Xiao helped the Traveler and Kaeya foil a plot against the Xiao Lantern materials. He refused to see the Mingxiao Lantern (that year it depicted Skybracer), calling it a fleeting human creation. When the Traveler brought the festival to him with a stall at the inn, he let himself be persuaded partway, then told the Traveler to watch the lanterns but call his name if danger came: he hears all cries for help and all the wishes the lanterns carry.

10.comment: Xiao: Osial and the battle of Liyue Harbor
10.content: When Childe released the ancient god Osial on Liyue Harbor (Chapter I, Act III), the adepti and Qixing fought together. Xiao, Ganyu and Madame Ping blessed the Traveler while Cloud Retainer, Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper manned the Guizhong Ballistas. When Osial smashed the platform, the adepti caught those who fell. Ningguang then dropped the Jade Chamber on the god. Keqing later thanked him for the fight; he remembered her blade.

11.comment: Xiao: Cloud Retainer and the adepti
11.content: The other adepti respect the Conqueror of Demons and call him by that title. In 1.0 he went to rouse Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper and Cloud Retainer after Rex Lapis's "death". Madame Ping hopes his oath has finally given him respite. Xianyun says he is even more withdrawn than she is.
